abstraction_design.rationale: The shared abstractions stretch to new cases (an Items page reuses api.js, format.js, Section, PokemonCard, pokemonRefsToSpecies wholesale); the copy-paste that remains is page scaffolding and card-list markup, not core logic.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + <ul class=cards> list pattern is duplicated in four pages (also app/app/page.jsx:60-65, app/app/abilities/[name]/page.jsx:40-49, app/app/types/[name]/page.jsx:73-80), so list-wide changes (sorting, empty states, layout) are edited four times.
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonCardList component that takes items and renders count + <ul>, with sort handled in the shared data helper.

findings.issue: Caching rules are split between the promise cache in lib/api.js:9-31 and six module-level memoized promises (data.js:9,20,28,48,56,73); changing caching semantics (e.g. TTL, invalidation) requires touching all of them.
findings.suggestion: Route every aggregate through one memoize(ttl, fn) helper in api.js so caching policy is a single implementation.

findings.issue: Client-side navigate() re-implements the query-param encoding rules that the server's queryString() (app/app/page.jsx:12-21) also implements, including the reset-to-page-1 rule living only client-side (HomeControls.jsx:37).
findings.suggestion: Share one param-encoding helper (or build URLs from a single source of truth) so the rules can't drift between server pagination links and client filter navigation.

findings.issue: MovesTable column keys must silently match the row-object shape produced by buildMoves in app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.jsx:103-118 — an implicit contract across a serialization boundary with no shared definition.
findings.suggestion: Define the column list once (in the data builder or a shared module) and derive both the columns and row keys from it.

findings.issue: The typeLabels.get(name) ?? humanize(name) fallback is repeated at four call sites; a missing-label bug would need four fixes.
findings.suggestion: Add a typeLabel(name, labels) helper (or have getTypeLabels return a function) used everywhere.

findings.issue: Each dynamic route repeats the get<Entity>() + generateMetadata + notFound + display-name scaffolding (abilities:12-25, moves:19-30, pokemon, types), which is what an Items route would copy too.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared resourcePage helper (fetch-by-name, metadata title, notFound) so new resource routes only supply the body markup.

findings.issue: entry.pokemon ?? entry silently accepts two different API entry shapes (ability/type wrap the ref in .pokemon), hiding a data-shape difference inside the generic helper.
findings.suggestion: Keep the helper single-shape and let call sites pass a small mapper, making the shape handling explicit per endpoint.

findings.issue: Plain JavaScript with no types anywhere (0 type lines); the implicit shapes of API responses and component props (e.g. the MovesTable row contract) are unverified, raising the cost of safe edits.
findings.suggestion: Adopt TypeScript, or at least JSDoc typedefs for the lib/data.js return shapes, so future edits to the derived data get checked.

summary: A small, well-factored App Router app with an exemplary server/client seam: all fetching sits behind lib/api.js and lib/data.js, and the two client components receive fully prepared serializable props. The main editability costs are duplicated page scaffolding — count+card-list markup in four pages, repeated metadata/getX boilerplate, and a four-fold type-label fallback — plus caching rules scattered across a promise cache and six module-level memoizations. Everything a future feature needs (an Items section, a new card list) has a clear home; it just sometimes requires editing N similar pages rather than one.
